text:
raj: kicking off AKS edge-rack bringup in eu-central for tenant=edge-retail. control plane on Azure Stack HCI, 2 GPU nodepools. starting now. anyone on call?

maria: oncall here. what node SKUs and CNI choice?

raj: plan: control plane on HCI, agent pools in Azure subscription. nodepools: gpu-a10 (3 x A10 v4), gpu-burst (1 spot for burst jobs). using Azure CNI + Calico for network policy. will enable containerd and nvidia-device-plugin.

kevin: FYI make sure kubelet cgroup driver=systemd on AKS-HCI images. we saw NotReady before when it was cgroupfs.

raj: noted. running initial commands:
```bash
az aks create --resource-group rg-edge-retail --name aks-edge-euc --location northeurope 
  --kubernetes-version 1.27.3 --network-plugin azure --network-policy calico 
  --node-vm-size Standard_ND40rs_v2 --node-count 3 
  --enable-addons monitoring,azure-policy --enable-msi
```

sasha: when you add GPU pool do: az aks nodepool add --cluster-name aks-edge-euc --name gpu-a10 --node-vm-size Standard_NVIDIA_A10_v4 --node-count 3 --labels gpu=true,workload=edge-inference

raj: created control plane and base agent pool. adding gpu-a10 now. hit an error during kubelet init on 1 node: node shows NotReady and kubelet logs show failed mount for blobfuse CSI.

kevin: paste the kubelet log snippet?

raj: log: 
"E0318 14:22:03.123456 1 kubelet_node_status.go:65] kubelet: failed to create csi mounter: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = mount failed: exit status 32: mount error(95): Operation not supported"

maria: blobfuse issue usually from missing fuse or kernel module in HCI image. Also confirm swap=off.

raj: verified swap=off. kernel modules list doesn't include fuse. Installing fuse package on the image, rebooting node.

devops-bot: deploy started: node/gpu-a10-2 -> healthcheck in progress :hourglass_flowing_sand:

raj: after reboot node comes Ready, nvidia-device-plugin daemonset failed initially (ImagePullBackOff). Turns out our private registry pull secret wasn't applied to the gpu nodepool.

sasha: you can patch daemonset to use imagePullSecrets: kubectl patch daemonset nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"acr-pull-secret"}]}}}}'

raj: patched, daemonset is running. validated GPUs visible: kubectl get nodes -o wide shows gpu-a10-0..2 Ready ; kubectl describe node gpu-a10-0 | grep -i nvidia -> device plugin registered 3 GPUs.

kevin: add autoscaler config next: cluster-autoscaler helm chart with scale-down disabled for edge workloads. also set taints/tolerations for burst pool.

raj: done. helm upgrade --install cluster-autoscaler <chart> --set awsRegion=unused \ --set azure.enabled=true --set autoscalingGroups[0].name=gpu-a10 --set autoscalingGroups[0].minSize=3 --set autoscalingGroups[0].maxSize=6

sre-oncall: ran kube-bench quick check and network policy tests. calico OK, but we need to enable egress lock-down in NSGs for storage endpoints.

maria: cost note: A10 nodes ~3x cost of standard compute; add budget alert and tag nodes with cost-center=edge-retail.

raj: handoff: control plane + gpu-a10 + gpu-burst created, metrics-server, cluster-autoscaler, calico, nvidia-device-plugin, blobfuse CSI installed. documented known post-boot actions in runbook: <https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/aks-edge-retail-euc>

kevin: I'll take handoff for day-2 ops. added myself to runbook owners. leaving a small checklist you can copy into ops:
- verify nodes Ready (kubectl get nodes)
- verify GPUs present (kubectl describe node | grep -i nvidia)
- check daemonsets in kube-system
- run sample inference pod with tolerations
- confirm autoscaler metrics
- ensure NSG egress rules to blob/storage

raj: thanks team :thumbsup: closing thread, will open infra ticket for image bake to include fuse + acr secrets by default.
